Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 1.4. Principle of equality before the law

1. persons who have committed administrative offences are equal before the law. individuals are subject to administrative liability irrespective of sex, race, ethnicity, language, origin, property status or official position, place of residence, attitude to religion, convictions, membership of public associations or other circumstances. legal entities are subject to administrative liability irrespective of their location, organisational and legal forms, subordination or other circumstances. article 1.4. principle of equality before the law

1. Persons who have committed administrative offences are equal before the law. Individuals are subject to administrative liability irrespective of sex, race, ethnicity, language, origin, property status or official position, place of residence, attitude to religion, convictions, membership of public associations or other circumstances. Legal entities are subject to administrative liability irrespective of their location, organisational and legal forms, subordination or other circumstances.

Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 1.5. Presumption of innocence
1. a person is subject to administrative liability only for administrative offences in respect of which that persons guilt has been established. article 1.5. presumption of innocence
1. A person is subject to administrative liability only for administrative offences in respect of which that person's guilt has been established.

2. a person against whom proceedings in an administrative offence case are being conducted is presumed innocent until that persons guilt has been proved in accordance with the procedure provided for by this code and established by a ruling that has entered into legal force, issued by the judge, body or official that heard the case. article 1.5. presumption of innocence

Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 2.1. Administrative offence

1. an administrative offence is an unlawful, culpable act (omission) of an individual or a legal entity for which administrative liability is established by this code or by the laws of constituent entities of the russian federation on administrative offences. article 2.1. administrative offence

1. An administrative offence is an unlawful, culpable act (omission) of an individual or a legal entity for which administrative liability is established by this Code or by the laws of constituent entities of the Russian Federation on administrative offences.

2. a legal entity is found guilty of committing an administrative offence if it is established that it had the opportunity to comply with the rules and standards for the breach of which administrative liability is provided for by this code or the laws of a constituent entity of the russian federation, but that entity did not take all measures within its power to comply with them. article 2.1. administrative offence

2. A legal entity is found guilty of committing an administrative offence if it is established that it had the opportunity to comply with the rules and standards for the breach of which administrative liability is provided for by this Code or the laws of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation, but that entity did not take all measures within its power to comply with them.

3. the imposition of an administrative penalty on a legal entity does not release the guilty individual from administrative liability for the offence, just as holding an individual administratively or criminally liable does not release the legal entity from administrative liability for the offence, except in the cases provided for by parts 4 and 5 of this article. article 2.1. administrative offence

3. The imposition of an administrative penalty on a legal entity does not release the guilty individual from administrative liability for the offence, just as holding an individual administratively or criminally liable does not release the legal entity from administrative liability for the offence, except in the cases provided for by parts 4 and 5 of this Article.

Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation. Article 22.3. Jurisdiction over administrative offence cases when bodies (official posts) authorized to consider them are abolished, reorganized or renamed

1. if a body, institution, its structural divisions or territorial bodies, or an official post specified in chapter 23 of this code or a law of a constituent entity of the russian federation is abolished, judges consider the administrative offence cases within its jurisdiction until the corresponding amendments and additions are made to this code or the law of the constituent entity of the russian federation. article 22.3. jurisdiction over administrative offence cases when bodies (official posts) authorized to consider them are abolished, reorganized or renamed

1. If a body, institution, its structural divisions or territorial bodies, or an official post specified in Chapter 23 of this Code or a law of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation is abolished, judges consider the administrative offence cases within its jurisdiction until the corresponding amendments and additions are made to this Code or the law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation.

2. if a body, institution, its structural divisions or territorial bodies specified in chapter 23 of this code or a law of a constituent entity of the russian federation is transformed, otherwise reorganized or placed under different authority, the body, institution, its structural divisions or territorial bodies to which those functions have been transferred consider the administrative offence cases within its jurisdiction until the corresponding amendments and additions are made to this code or the law of the constituent entity of the russian federation. article 22.3. jurisdiction over administrative offence cases when bodies (official posts) authorized to consider them are abolished, reorganized or renamed

1. district (city) commissions and district commissions within cities for minors affairs and the protection of their rights shall hear cases concerning administrative offences committed by minors, as well as cases concerning administrative offences provided for by articles 5.35, 5.36, 6.10, 6.23 and 20.22 of this code. article 23.2. commissions for minors affairs and the protection of their rights

1. District (city) commissions and district commissions within cities for minors' affairs and the protection of their rights shall hear cases concerning administrative offences committed by minors, as well as cases concerning administrative offences provided for by Articles 5.35, 5.36, 6.10, 6.23 and 20.22 of this Code.

2. cases concerning administrative offences in the field of road traffic shall be heard by commissions for minors affairs and the protection of their rights where the authority or official to whom the case concerning such an administrative offence has been submitted refers it to that commission for consideration. article 23.2. commissions for minors affairs and the protection of their rights

2. Cases concerning administrative offences in the field of road traffic shall be heard by commissions for minors' affairs and the protection of their rights where the authority or official to whom the case concerning such an administrative offence has been submitted refers it to that commission for consideration.

1. a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held must be complied with by the person held administratively liable. article 32.14. enforcement of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held
1. A ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held must be complied with by the person held administratively liable.

2. the federal executive body responsible for internal affairs shall maintain a list of persons subjected to the type of administrative penalty specified in part 1 of this article, to ensure enforcement of rulings imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held (hereinafter, the list of persons). article 32.14. enforcement of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held

2. The federal executive body responsible for internal affairs shall maintain a list of persons subjected to the type of administrative penalty specified in part 1 of this article, to ensure enforcement of rulings imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held (hereinafter, the list of persons).

3. the federal executive body responsible for internal affairs shall enter information in the list of persons no later than three working days from the day it receives a copy of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held that has entered into force. article 32.14. enforcement of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held

3. The federal executive body responsible for internal affairs shall enter information in the list of persons no later than three working days from the day it receives a copy of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held that has entered into force.

4. a person shall be deemed removed from the list of persons upon expiry of the administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held, or when the federal executive body responsible for internal affairs has received a judicial act that has entered into force quashing the ruling imposing that administrative ban. article 32.14. enforcement of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held

5. the federal executive body responsible for internal affairs shall remove information from the list of persons no later than three working days following the day the administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held expires, or no later than three working days from the day it receives a copy of a judicial act that has entered into force quashing the ruling imposing that administrative ban. article 32.14. enforcement of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held

The federal executive body responsible for internal affairs shall remove information from the list of persons no later than three working days following the day the administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held expires, or no later than three working days from the day it receives a copy of a judicial act that has entered into force quashing the ruling imposing that administrative ban.

6. the information contained in the list of persons (the surname, given name, patronymic (if any), date and place of birth of the person in respect of whom the courts decision imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held has entered into legal force; the date and number of that court decision; and the dates on which the administrative penalty begins and expires) shall be open to public inspection. article 32.14. enforcement of a ruling imposing an administrative ban on attending venues of official sporting competitions on the days they are held
